facility_roles.quote: The Fly’s eye experiment consisted of two detectors ( F.E. I and F.E. II ) located at Dugway Proving Ground (40 o North) in Utah.

intervals.label: Fly's Eye operating
intervals.note: Sokolsky & Thomson (arXiv:0706.1248) say "The detectors were operated from 1982 to 1992"; Bertou et al. (astro-ph/0001516) say data taking "started ... in 1982". The Fly's Eye group's own final paper says 1981, used here; the start-year disagreement is recorded in the log.

intervals.label: data taking ended
intervals.note: Start is the end year of the original experiment; HiRes succeeded it on the same site.

each mirror having a diameter of 1.5 meters
The Fly's Eye is a compound eye of 880 photomultiplier tube (PMT) pixels

key_specs.label: Separation of Fly's Eye I and II

quantity.quote: The two detectors were spaced 3.4 km apart.

name: Fly's Eye
notes: No named Fly's Eye collaboration appears in the sources read (authors are listed by institution, mainly the University of Utah and the University of Illinois), so no collaboration record is created.
Start of data taking: 1981 (Bird et al. 1998) versus 1982 (Sokolsky & Thomson 2007; Bertou et al. 2000); see the log.
The 15 October 1991 shower (about 3.2 × 10²⁰ eV) is recorded as result:flys-eye-highest-energy-cosmic-ray-1995.
Fly's Eye I and II are not separately located: the sources give only about 40 N, 113 W (site:dugway-flys-eye is an approximate region marker).

physics_goals.quote: A Greisen-Zatsepin-Kuz'min cutoff of the energy spectrum (due to pion photoproduction energy losses) should occur below this energy unless the highest energy cosmic rays have traveled less than about 30 Mpc.
physics_goals.value: Measure the cosmic-ray energy spectrum at the highest energies and test for the Greisen-Zatsepin-Kuzmin cutoff.

summary.plain: The original Fly's Eye was a battery of mirrors and light sensors in the Utah desert that watched the night sky for the faint ultraviolet glow of cosmic-ray air showers. In 1991 it recorded the most energetic cosmic ray ever seen, about 3 × 10²⁰ eV.
summary.technical: First-generation air-fluorescence cosmic-ray detector on the Dugway Proving Ground, Utah: Fly's Eye I (67 mirrors of 1.5 m diameter, 880 PMT pixels imaging the whole sky; built 1978-1981, operated 1981/82-1992) and Fly's Eye II (36 mirrors, 3.3-3.4 km away) for stereo. Recorded a 320 EeV (3.2 × 10²⁰ eV) shower on 15 October 1991. Succeeded by HiRes.
